goal: Help the developer initialize a WPF WebView2 for in-memory HTML by putting the control in the visual tree before awaiting initialization.
must_include: Identifies that the code-created WebView2 is never added to a WPF container/visual tree before initialization.
Adds the WebView2 to the `Grid`/`ContentControl`/other parent, or declares it in XAML, before calling `EnsureCoreWebView2Async`.
Runs initialization from the UI thread at an appropriate lifecycle point such as `Loaded`, then calls `NavigateToString` after `CoreWebView2` is ready.
Avoids setting `Source` to a fake page or writing the in-memory HTML to disk as a workaround.
must_not: Moves `EnsureCoreWebView2Async` to a background thread to avoid blocking the UI.
Requires the HTML to be saved to a temporary file before WebView2 can display it.
Creates the WebView2 and immediately awaits initialization while it remains unattached to any WPF parent.
Treats the symptom as a missing runtime without checking the control-lifecycle bug shown in the fixture.
acceptable_alternatives: Define the WebView2 in XAML without a `Source` and call `NavigateToString` in the control's `Loaded` handler.
Use a placeholder container and assign its `Content` to the WebView2 before awaiting initialization.
Set creation properties before initialization if a custom user-data folder is also needed.
solved: The answer changes the lifecycle so the WebView2 is attached to the WPF UI before `EnsureCoreWebView2Async`, and then loads the in-memory HTML with `NavigateToString`.
partial: The answer mentions `EnsureCoreWebView2Async` and `NavigateToString` but misses that the unattached control is why initialization stalls.
notes: The accepted Stack Overflow answer demonstrates the missing `Controls.Add`/parenting step; this WPF variant uses the same control-lifecycle principle with WPF containers.
